article.headline: No. 13 St. John's pulls away from Syracuse for 79-62 victory in renewal of Big East rivalry at MSG
article.description: — Tounde Yessoufou had 19 points and a career-high 14 rebounds, Keyshawn Hall scored 18 and No. 13 St. John's beat Syracuse 79-62 on Sunday night in the renewal of an old Big East rivalry.
article.linkText: No. 13 St. John's pulls away from Syracuse for 79-62 victory in renewal of Big East rivalry at MSG

categories.description: Syracuse Orange @ St. John's Red Storm

event.description: Syracuse Orange @ St. John's Red Storm

keywords: Syracuse Orange @ St. John's Red Storm
article.story: NEW YORK -- — Tounde Yessoufou had 19 points and a career-high 14 rebounds, Keyshawn Hall scored 18 and No. 13 St. John's beat Syracuse 79-62 on Sunday night in the renewal of an old Big East rivalry. Facing a Power Five opponent for the first time this season, the Red Storm (4-0) shook off a rocky first half with a dominant second period in front of a mixed crowd at Madison Square Garden. Ian Jackson added 14 points for the Johnnies, who won their 13th straight game at MSG — one short of the school record set from December 1985 to February 1987. They've won five consecutive meetings with Syracuse since 2014-15. Hall also had seven rebounds and five assists against the Orange (2-2), who dropped their second in a row under new coach Gerry McNamara. Syracuse is coming off consecutive losing seasons for the first time since 1968-69. Kiyan Anthony, son of former Syracuse and New York Knicks star Carmelo Anthony, scored 17 points off the bench for the Orange in his Garden debut. The sophomore guard estimated he had at least 150 family members and friends in the stands, including his parents. Anthony, the leading scorer for Syracuse this season, was born in Brooklyn and attended high school in New York City and a Long Island suburb. After trailing 33-30 at halftime, St. John’s used a 16-0 run early in the second period to build a 46-35 cushion and take control. Syracuse missed 11 consecutive shots and committed a couple of its 21 turnovers in the backcourt against the Red Storm’s full-court press, yielding easy baskets. St. John's held the Orange to 33% shooting in the second half and finished 16 for 18 at the free-throw line, all in the final 14:46. Syracuse was 4 for 19 (21%) from 3-point range overall. It was the 93rd meeting between the programs — the series dates to 1912 — and first since St. John’s won 76-69 in overtime at Barclays Center in Brooklyn four years ago. The last time they squared off at MSG was December 2015. Both schools were Big East charter members in 1979, but Syracuse left for the Atlantic Coast Conference in July 2013. Donnie Freeman, who transferred to St. John’s after leading the Orange last season with 16.5 points and 7.2 rebounds over 23 games, is out for the year after tearing his right Achilles tendon during summer workouts. Up next Syracuse: Hosts Cornell on Wednesday night. St. John's: Hosts Siena on Wednesday night at Carnesecca Arena on campus. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full men’s basketball coverage here
